user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised, open‑label trial of a GPRC5D‑targeted bispecific antibody in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after 2–4 prior lines, including a proteasome inhibitor and lenalidomide. The drug is given subcutaneously with step‑up dosing in Cycle 1. The trial will enrol patients globally, with sites in the US, Europe, and South Korea. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will submit to NICE. Our TPP aims to demonstrate superiority in disease‑related bone pain, physical function, and overall HRQoL. We also need to capture treatment tolerability, CRS symptoms, and taste disturbances. Please generate a full COA strategy.
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This GPRC5D-targeted bispecific antibody trial requires a comprehensive PRO strategy focused on disease-related symptoms and treatment tolerability, grounded in EORTC QLQ-C30/MY20 precedent from five daratumumab Phase 3 trials and regulatory expectations for unbiased open-label assessment [CT-001].

**Key challenge:**  Open-label bias poses the greatest regulatory risk for this trial, requiring extensive advance planning with justification of unbiased instrument selection and support from objective measures, as mandated by EMA guidelines for PRO data in uncontrolled designs.  This is particularly critical for symptom-specific claims (bone pain, taste disturbances, CRS) where blinding is impossible and patient expectations may influence reporting patterns.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 plus QLQ-MY20 provides the foundation used in four of five daratumumab comparator trials [CT-001][CT-003][CT-004][CT-005], complemented by EQ-5D-5L for HTA requirements [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003][CT-004].  This combination satisfies EMA requirements for hypothesis-led strategy with scientifically rational instrument selection and includes sensitive multidimensional HRQoL assessment to capture both benefits and potential negative effects across domains. 

**Critical gap:** No validated instrument specifically captures cytokine release syndrome symptoms or taste disturbances in MM patients — the QLQ-MY20 contains one taste item but comprehensive CRS assessment requires novel item development or validated symptom scales from CAR-T literature [TI-005].

## Key Observations

• **Five daratumumab comparator trials establish EORTC QLQ-C30 as the core instrument for MM PRO assessment, with significant pain and physical function improvements detected in APOLLO and AQUILA but not ALCYONE** [CT-001][CT-003][CT-004].
• **EQ-5D-5L utility data supported positive outcomes in 4/5 comparator trials, providing critical precedent for HTA submissions and cost-effectiveness analysis** [CT-001][CT-002][CT-004][CT-005].
• **Open-label design creates substantial regulatory risk requiring extensive justification of instrument selection and objective measure support per EMA guidance** [RULE-005].
• **Translation limitations pose the greatest operational challenge: QLQ-MY20 has ~70 languages but limited Asian coverage may delay trial initiation in South Korea** [Table 5].
• **No validated instrument captures cytokine release syndrome symptoms specific to bispecific antibody mechanisms, creating a critical measurement gap for this drug class** [TI-005].
• **FACT/GOG-NTX provides neuropathy assessment established in taxane trials but uncertain relevance to GPRC5D-specific neurological effects** [TI-004].

## Comparator Analysis

All five daratumumab comparator trials (CD38-targeted monoclonal antibody) used EORTC QLQ-C30 as the primary PRO instrument, with APOLLO and AQUILA additionally incorporating QLQ-MY20 for MM-specific symptoms [CT-003][CT-004]. Significant improvements in pain were detected in APOLLO (p<0.001) and AQUILA using QLQ-C30, while physical function benefits were demonstrated in both trials [CT-003][CT-004]. EQ-5D-5L utility improvements supported positive outcomes in ALCYONE, ANDROMEDA, and AQUILA, providing regulatory precedent for utility-based claims [CT-001][CT-002][CT-004]. If the current trial aims to demonstrate superiority in disease-related bone pain and physical function, using EORTC QLQ-C30 — the same instrument that detected change in APOLLO and AQUILA — would allow direct cross-trial comparison in regulatory submissions. This is a recognised regulatory strategy per [FDA PRO Guidance 2009](https://www.fda.gov/media/77832/download). The QLQ-C30 is best supported by same-class comparators for bone pain assessment across 5 trials.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument & Version | Preferred Value Set | Current Battery Status | Risk if Omitted |
|----------|------------------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | England 5L value set | In candidates | QALY calculation impossible; NICE will issue a Request for Additional Data, delaying reimbursement by ≥12 months |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to use EORTC QLQ-C30 as the primary PRO given its use in all 5 daratumumab comparator trials (Table 1, [CT-001]-[CT-005]) but potential ceiling effects in physical function domains (Table 3).

2. Whether to include EORTC QLQ-MY20 for disease-specific symptom capture given its validation in MM and taste item relevance to TPP, versus accepting the severe translation limitation requiring 6-12 month Korean localization (Table 5, [TI-005]).

3. Assessment schedule frequency: adopt the APOLLO/AQUILA every-cycle schedule (Table 2, [CT-003][CT-004]) versus reduced frequency given subcutaneous administration weekly dosing and step-up requirements that may increase patient burden per [RULE-012].

4. Endpoint hierarchy: pre-specify bone pain response versus physical function as the key secondary PRO endpoint, given APOLLO showed significant pain improvement (HR not reported, p<0.001) while physical function results varied across trials (Table 4, [CT-003][CT-004]).

5. Whether to commission novel CRS symptom items or adapt validated scales from CAR-T literature, given no existing MM-validated instrument captures cytokine release syndrome per TPP requirements and [RULE-008] mandates validated instruments appropriate for the research objective.
